SchemaFactory now keys its schema and property caches on a process-wide static, scoped by a cacheScope computed in the constructor. Added SchemaFactory::flushCache() for workers and test isolation.

CORRECTION to this issue's premise: the scope does NOT need the JsonSchemaParser tool name/description. schemaConverter is only used on the CanProvideJsonSchema branch of schema(), which returns before the cache is consulted, and makeSchema()/getPropertySchemas() never touch it - so parser configuration cannot reach a cached value. schemaRenderer is likewise only used by render()/toArray(). Scoping on either would have silently stopped custom-configured factories from sharing, i.e. defeated the fix for exactly the callers it targets. The only input that qualifies is useObjectReferences. I built a CanProvideCacheScope interface on the original premise and then removed it once the data flow disproved it.

Extra hazard found and handled: getPropertySchemas() runs inside makeObjectSchema()'s recursion guard, so a schema built at expansion depth >= 2 is truncated. Per-request factories re-derived that each time; a process-wide cache would let whichever traversal ran first win forever. The cache key now includes the live expansion state (empty string for every top-level lookup, so no cost in the common case).

Existing SchemaFactoryDefaultSingletonRegressionTest asserted the private $schemaCache was not shared - the exact behaviour this changes. Rewrote it: the fresh-instance guard stays (that is the real singleton concern, since inlineObjectExpansionDepth is mutable), and it now pins that differently-configured factories do not collide, identically-configured ones do share, and flushCache() drops entries. Schema is a readonly class with no mutators, so shared entries cannot carry state between callers.

Fixed one layer down from where this issue pointed. Measured breakdown of LLMConfig::fromPreset('openai') at 82.0 us total:
  BasePath::resolveExisting   8.1 us
  Config::fromPaths           1.2 us
  load()->toArray()          70.5 us   <- 86%
  fromArray()                 0.7 us

So memoizing fromPreset itself would have cached the cheap part. Config::load() now memoizes the parsed file process-wide, keyed by path + mtime. Result: load() 70.5 -> 4.4 us, fromPreset total 82.0 -> 15.1 us (5.4x). This also benefits every other config group, not just llm.

Two correctness properties the memo has to hold, both covered by the new ConfigSourceMemoRegressionTest:
  - Env placeholders must NOT be frozen. Config::load() memoizes readSource() output, which is pre-template; $this->template->resolveData() still runs on every load, so ${VAR} sees current env.
  - A config file edited mid-process must be picked up. mtime is part of the key, costing one stat per load.
Added Config::flushSourceCache() for workers and for tests that rewrite files faster than mtime resolution.

Did NOT memoize BasePath::resolveExisting (the remaining 8.1 us): caching directory existence risks stale negative results if a config dir appears mid-process, and 8 us against a 2.7 ms request is not worth that.

WONTFIX - premise does not hold at real SSE shapes.

Measured the implode/explode round-trip on the 943-event long_streaming_stress cassette: events average 1.00 lines each, so the round-trip costs 0.050 us per event = 0.047 ms per stream, which is 0.36% of a 13.2 ms inference_stream. There is nothing meaningful to reclaim.

Against that, removing it means changing the signatures of protected readSseEvents()/processSseEvent(). PHP treats adding even an optional parameter to an overridable method as a BC break, and these are protected on a released 2.6.0 class. Not worth a BC risk for 0.36%.

Semantics verified rather than assumed. StreamingUsageState::apply() returns early on null, but that early return also skips the $this->isCumulative ||= $isCumulative line, so the flag now flips at the final delta instead of the first. isCumulative() has no callers anywhere in the repo, and mid-stream totals are all-zero either way, so this is unobservable. End-of-stream accumulated usage verified byte-identical across both arms on the real cassette: {input:1536, output:940, cacheWrite:0, cacheRead:1408, reasoning:0}.

readSseEvents() now maintains the two implicit-boundary predicates incrementally instead of rescanning the buffered lines per incoming line.

The quadratic is real but narrower than this issue described. It is NOT reachable via accumulating data lines: a standalone data line triggers a flush, so the buffer stays at one element, and a non-standalone continuation line early-returns before any scan. The reachable shape is a relay emitting 'event:' lines with no data line and no blank separators - hasDataLine() then full-scans a buffer that never flushes. Measured, confirming O(n^2): n=500 2.51 ms, 1000 7.26 ms, 2000 29.70 ms, 4000 117.20 ms.

After: n=500 0.57, 1000 0.37, 2000 0.99, 4000 3.00 ms. Linear; 39x at n=4000.

Per this issue's instruction, behaviour was pinned before the change: snapshotted parser output across 12 SSE shapes (well-formed, no-blank-line relay, event-then-data, multi-line data with and without blank separators, comments, event-only, mixed id/event fields, trailing partial, CRLF, data-with-no-space, leading blanks) and diffed after - byte-identical on all 12. Those shapes are now EventStreamReaderBoundaryScalingRegressionTest, together with a growth-ratio assertion (asserts on the 1000->4000 ratio, not wall-clock, so it is not a machine-speed benchmark).

hasDataLine()/isStandaloneDataEvent()/shouldFlushImplicitBoundary() are kept as the readable definition of the predicates; the hot path routes through a private O(1) equivalent.

Event ids now come from Uuid::correlationId() — a per-process CSPRNG prefix plus a counter — instead of a fresh random_bytes(16) per event.

Counter masked to 60 bits so the string length is fixed forever rather than silently going invalid on overflow. Uuid::uuid4() untouched.
- packages/events/src/Event.php: $this->id = Uuid::correlationId()

Measured: 0.245 us vs 0.594 us per draw over 100k (2.4x). new HttpResponseChunkReceived x822 fell 0.70 -> 0.37 ms; layer benchmark row A 1.25 -> 0.89 ms.

Security note kept in the method docblock: within a process these ids are guessable (low 60 bits are a counter). They are correlation ids for logs/traces/events only — never authorization, addressing, or anything an attacker benefits from predicting. Documented fork caveat: a process forking AFTER its first call shares prefix and counter with the child; children should call resetCorrelationPrefix(). The pid is mixed into the prefix so a child that first calls after forking is already distinct.

LaravelHttpResponseAdapter now dispatches the documented payload shape and carries a requestId.

Root cause confirmed: the adapter dispatched 'new HttpResponseChunkReceived($chunk)' with a raw string. HttpClientTelemetryProjector::onChunkReceived() does EventData::string($data, 'requestId') and EventData::string($data, 'chunk') and returns early when either is null, so every streamed chunk under the Laravel driver was invisible to telemetry and had no correlation id.

- LaravelPool: left at the default — it builds the adapter with streaming: false, so stream() never runs, and it has no HttpRequest in scope at that point
